hints.title: State Extension Rules
hints.text: A '1' can always be appended to any valid prefix.

hints.title: Adjacent Zero Invariant
hints.text: A '0' can only be appended if the current prefix is empty or its last character is '1'.

hints.title: Backtracking Base Case
hints.text: When the prefix reaches length n, append it to the result list.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def validStrings(self, n: int) -> list[str]:
        ans = []
        def dfs(path):
            if len(path) == n:
                ans.append("".join(path))
                return
            path.append('1')
            dfs(path)
            path.pop()
            if not path or path[-1] == '1':
                path.append('0')
                dfs(path)
                path.pop()
        dfs([])
        return ans
```

complexity.notes: Number of valid strings without consecutive zeros follows the Fibonacci sequence.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all 2^n binary strings and filtering takes unnecessary work.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Prune recursive branches early to generate only valid strings.
